name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Deliver: Push link coverage toward 100% at +5%/day (the access gate)

name: Reel
text: To push link coverage toward 100% at +5%/day, I recommend we prioritize reviewing and transcribing the most critical and frequently accessed sections of the content first. This decision allows us to maximize the impact of our daily progress, ensuring that the most important information is readily available. By focusing on high-priority sections, we accept the trade-off of potentially delaying the transcription of less critical content, but this approach will ultimately lead to a more significant increase in overall link coverage. This focused approach will help us achieve our daily goal of +5% link coverage increase, moving us closer to the 100% target.

name: Scriv
text: Scriv here. Reel’s plan risks chasing the wrong "critical" links—what’s *frequently accessed* today may not be the *gating links* for tomorrow’s bus task. Instead, we should map the dependency graph of the bus task *first*, then target the links that *block* it. That’s the only way to guarantee the +5%/day coverage actually unlocks the next step. Settle it by showing me the dependency chain—if Reel can’t produce it, we’re guessing.
